title: The Missing Layer After Launch - Raphael Kalandadze, Wandero AI
talk_summary: Raphael argues that the real work starts after launch: you need a closed feedback loop that watches production agent behavior, diagnoses problems, and ships fixes. He describes three layers he built at Wandero AI — an hourly log-monitoring agent that opens PRs, a weekly session-analyzer that scores conversation health, and a computer-use agent that simulates users — all feeding a separate fresh-context review agent before humans see anything.

takeaways.technique: Hourly log-monitoring agent that opens PRs
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent runs every 15-60 minutes over the last window of production logs/trajectories, has codebase access, diagnoses whether users got stuck, and either opens a PR with a rich description or sends a Slack alert for critical issues.
takeaways.numbers: PR ready in half an hour

takeaways.technique: Separate fresh-context critic agent on auto-generated PRs
takeaways.what_they_do: The diagnosing agent is eager to fix and biased toward its own theory, so a second agent with fresh context reviews the PR from a different angle, runs focused tests, and can request changes or close the PR outright before a human sees it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We prefer to have a separate agent which has a like fresh context. It try to check um the PR on different angle

takeaways.what_they_do: A batch agent scores every production conversation on success/sentiment/tool-call counts and produces ranked sessions plus cross-session 'AI insights' (pattern, root cause, affected sessions, recommended fix) on a weekly cadence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can have a system that helps you to to score every conversations, understand what's happening and give you a high-level summary of the system

takeaways.what_they_do: A browser agent logs into the product and simulates customer flows to catch UI-level problems that logs and code review miss; they sped it up by giving it a skill that knows their DOM instead of generic browsing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have some computer use agent that helps you to uh to open the browser, uh to log in, and try to simulate the customer itself

takeaways.technique: Give the ops agent full human-equivalent access
takeaways.what_they_do: The monitoring agents get trajectories, metrics, database, UI, and codebase access — the same context a human debugger would need — so diagnoses are grounded rather than guessed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to give access to all the kind of tools that is needed. So, you need to have a lot of trajectories and metrics, database, UI

takeaways.technique: Close the loop before removing humans
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately kept a human gate while the loop was uncalibrated, arguing you should first make the human the bottleneck and then remove them once the loop is trusted; their agents already produce ~10x the PRs of the 3-person team.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let's make the problem when you are the bottleneck and then you can remove yourself pretty easily
